title: Why Claude Thornhill was in California; his arranging gifts
summary: Hughes checks Claude's whereabouts; Maxine praises his blending of brass and reeds and his skeleton arrangements.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: There's just a couple of other small points. One is that, we were speculating about why Claude Thornhill might've been in California in 1939 on the first session.
Yeah. I couldn't figure out why he was there except for the fact that he might've been out there in the service.
But he didn't actually join the Navy Band which was directed by Artie Shaw until 1942. I looked that up. It's true his successful band was established in '46.
Yeah.
But he did have some sort of a band from '40 to '42 both on the east and west coast. I don't know if it was just a recording outfit

Well you see, as I've mentioned before, because of Claude's studio affiliation, it would have been easy for him to have gotten a group of musicians together and recorded or whatever.
Claude basically was a very good arranger, because he arranged for Andre Kostelanetz. He was very much in demand as an arranger.
Claude --
And he had the talent for picking other good arrangers too.
Yeah.
He hired Gil Evans.
That's right.
Well he knew what he wanted in the way of --
Even in those little skeleton arrangements that he made for me, they're definitely Claude Thornhill.
He had a way of blending instruments outside of the usual stock arrangement -- you know,

Well, I've seen some references to the fact that he did studio work out there among other things.
